thread.title: Qorvo In A Tricky Spot Between Opportunity And Execution - Qorvo, Inc (NASDAQ:QRVO)

author: Stephen Simpson, CFA
title: Qorvo In A Tricky Spot Between Opportunity And Execution - Qorvo, Inc (NASDAQ:QRVO)
text:
One of the most frustrating investment situations to be in is when a company has exciting potential and large market opportunities, but just can’t marry that to sustained execution. It’s been a while since I’ve written publicly on Qorvo ( QRVO ), but inconsistent execution was an issue in late 2016 and it remains an issue today, even though there are a lot of legitimate positive points to this story.
Winning business from Apple ( AAPL ) that was previously Broadcom ’s ( AVGO ) domain was a coup, and I like the company’s strong position in GaN semiconductors, as well as the growth opportunities in the IDP business. I don’t like the disappointing, inconsistent, “it’s always something” track record with gross margins, and it’s a significant impediment to Qorvo realizing its full potential. Even so, I’m intrigued by the potential value here and I think the stock price may be underpinned by a sense of “if they won’t fix it … somebody else will” M&A leverage.
Mobile Coming Along Although there remains a meaningful dichotomy between the world of RF components for high-end phones (where Broadcom has traditionally been strong) and low-to-mid-range phones (where Skyworks ( SWKS ) has made its name), Qorvo has managed to navigate both and continue to grow its mobile business. Qorvo has broad exposure to multiple components, including power amplifiers, switches, and filters, as well as combined front-end modules that tie them together in convenient integrated packages for smartphone OEMs.
Qorvo has long been the only company to offer filter products across the board, from the low/mid-range end (SAW filters and TC-SAW filters) to the high-end BAW filters. More recently, though, the company’s BAW filter business (underpinned by its SMR technology) has been gaining share on Broadcom, moving from around 25% to 35% of the market to more in the range of 35% to 40%.
Qorvo looks poised for more growth in mobile. Although high-end smartphone demand has been weaker than expected recently, ongoing adoption of carrier aggregation, LTE Advanced, and 4x4 MIMO should continue to drive increased content in areas like advanced filtering, antenna tuning, and envelope tracking, which means more unit revenue growth potential for Qorvo. The company has also had some success growing its business with Apple – securing a sizable piece of mid/high-band PAD in Apple’s LCD phones (likely around 50%).
Mobile is about two-thirds of Qorvo’s revenue mix, and I like the outlook for double-digit industry content growth over the next three to five years, with the aforementioned LTE Advanced, 4x4 MIMO, and eventually 5G driving the market opportunity. Qorvo’s recent win with Apple was encouraging, but the company needs to get some additional premium wins to really reassure investors, particularly as Broadcom is not going to be an easy rival to dislodge.
IDP Poised For More Growth It’s impossible to argue that Mobile isn’t important for Qorvo given the revenue it represents, but the shares sometimes trade as if Qorvo were only a mobile/Apple supplier story. Qorvo’s Infrastructure and Defense Products (or IDP) business is a quality business in its own right, and one I expect will continue to offer good growth and margins.
IDP is built around a range of RF components largely for applications in communications and defense, with Qorvo historically having meaningfully exposure to cellular base stations and defense applications (the company has had around $100K of content on most fighter jets). Between content growth and market unit volume growth, management is looking for the base station addressable market to grow from about $350 million in 2017 to $1.5 billion in 2022, while the defense opportunity grows from around $1.1 billion to $1.7 billion over the same timeframe.
The biggest incremental opportunity may be in IoT, though, as management believes its addressable market will triple from about $1.2 billion in 2017. Not surprisingly, given Qorvo’s core operations in RF products, the company is focused on the wireless communication side of IoT, with ultra-low power front-end products like amplifiers and filters for Bluetooth, Zigbee, WiFi, and LTE. Qorvo’s focus on the communications side will put it into competition with companies like Skyworks, Silicon Labs ( SLAB ), and Texas Instruments ( TXN ) in at least some cases, and Qorvo does not have the capabilities in microcontrollers and other IoT components that Silicon Labs and TI have. Still, Qorvo isn’t looking to address all opportunities and there is likely to be plenty of “mix and match” product/component adoption as the IoT market develops and matures. Said differently, even with a somewhat limited line-up relative to some players, I think there’s room for Qorvo to win business in IoT.
The Opportunity Qorvo reminds me a little bit of the old Broadcom (before Avago acquired it), at least insofar as the market often taking a narrow view of the company that doesn’t go much beyond the near-term outlook for the mobile business. Like old Broadcom, I think investors sometimes overlook the quality non-mobile business. In the case of Broadcom, it was the company’s capabilities in switching/routing and ASICs, while for Qorvo it is the company’s strong technology in GaN chips and the opportunity to drive non-mobile revenue growth from that platform.
Unfortunately, though, consistent operational excellence remains an issue and an aspiration goal at Qorvo. Management has been targeting 50%-plus gross margins for several years now, but seems unable to break out above the high 40%’s despite a growing high-end BAW business, greater use of 8” wafers, and so on. I cannot say whether Qorvo will ever get its ducks in a row here, but I believe the operating margin potential is strong (30%-35%) if they can. I also believe that this is a window of potential M&A opportunity – I could see a larger semiconductor company being attracted by the end-market growth in Qorvo’s served markets and the opportunity to drive powerful earnings synergy with better manufacturing/GM execution.
On its own, I think Qorvo can drive high single-digit revenue growth through ongoing content growth in mobile (particularly with growing relevance/competitiveness on the high end), with low double-digit FCF growth. I am assuming that GMs (and thus OPMs) get better from here, and maybe that’s a bullish/aggressive assumption, though I’m not expecting the company to hit management’s targets.
Qorvo shares would appear to be undervalued on a cash flow basis, with a suggested annualized return in the low double-digits. The shares also look undervalued on a margin-driven EV/revenue basis, with a near-term fair value near $90 and upside toward $100 if/when the margin improvement story becomes more believable.
The Bottom Line I’m frankly skeptical of any semiconductor stock that looks meaningfully undervalued today, and it leads me to question if and/or where I’m being too optimistic. In the case of Qorvo, the company has certainly seen some pushback from weaker-than-expected market demand for high-end smartphones, and ongoing skepticism about GM execution). I think that skepticism might be overdone, though, and this looks like an interesting name to consider even at this relatively late point in the cycle. That said, the ongoing trade dispute with China is a growing concern as of this writing and it injects a lot more uncertainty into the story. I can understand waiting to see how it all sorts out, and there are certainly potential negative consequences, but I think there will be some resolution that spares the long-term opportunities for Qorvo.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AVGO.
